card.name: Hedging words in old scholarly prose
card.fires_on: The word "somewhat", and sometimes "will", "would" or "served", in older 19th-century scientific or antiquarian writing. It comes mid-sentence, right before an adjective or verb that continues a hedged claim.

modes.label: somewhat before adjective
modes.description: The hedge "somewhat" sits before a describing word in a descriptive aside.
modes.example: It is isolated as a yellowish metal,<< somewhat>> malleable but harder than calcium.

modes.label: will/would in argument
modes.description: A modal verb in formal old prose announcing what will be shown or what is probable.
modes.example: Several of the conclusions<< will>> be supported by original experiments.

modes.label: served as verb
modes.description: A past-tense verb in a report of what others claimed.
